rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the legal discussion, saying “Enter it in peace” counts as Quran recitation when intended as Quran; without that intention the speaker is not a Quran reciter.
rows.anchor: على غير قصد بقارىء للقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bodily worship generally opposes desire, chiefly appetite for food and sex, though people may have no other appetites.
rows.anchor: فإن أحدا لا يخلو عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The birds people desire in Paradise are wanted from pure appetite, not need or necessity; this distinction was explained earlier in the sūra.
rows.anchor: أي لا يكون لحاجة ولا ضرورة بل لمجرد الشهوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sexual appetite remains desire, or at most a need rather than a necessity, so it is always pure desire.
rows.anchor: وأما شهوة الفرج فلا تخرج عن كونها شهوة وإن خرجت تكون في محل الحاجة لا الضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sexual desire is never detached from bodily worship: intercourse invalidates pilgrimage, fasting, and prayer; eating invalidates fasting and prayer, but not pilgrimage and perhaps not prayer.
rows.anchor: حكم الشارع ببطلان الحج به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Passing waste signals satisfaction of appetite for food, while semen emission signals sexual gratification; both therefore call for purification of the soul, with outward and inward purification corresponding.
rows.anchor: خروج الخارج دليل قضاء الشهوة البطنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A perceptive person finds lightness and eagerness for prayer and remembrance when purifying the inward self during the ritual bath after sexual impurity.
rows.anchor: فإنه يجد خفة ورغبة في الصلاة والذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although eating satisfies appetite, it does not itself establish pure desire because food may answer need or necessity; penetration is always desire and never necessity.
rows.anchor: الأكل قد يكون لحاجة وضرورة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet’s saying “water is only from water” makes seminal emission the basis for the ritual bath, just as discharge is the basis for ablution; after emission sexual desire ordinarily subsides.
rows.anchor: ( إنما الماء من الماء ) فإن الإنزال كالإحداث

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report prescribes ablution after food touched by fire; cooked food indicates gratification rather than urgent necessity, just as bodily discharge indicates appetite.
rows.anchor: الوضوء من أكل ما مسته النار

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī treats sexual appetite as pure desire that cannot accompany worship during major impurity, so a sexually impure person should not recite Quran; minor impurity is not caused by pure desire, so its subject may recite.
rows.anchor: فالشافعي رضي الله عنه قضى بأن شهوة الفرج شهوة محضة

none: Quran text only; no commentary point is given.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that God knowingly created people who would persist in disbelief does not disprove wisdom: every divine act is wise, even when its wisdom is unknown to us.
rows.anchor: علمنا أن أفعاله كلها على وفق الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apparently misshapen or ugly people do not refute that God made human forms beautiful: beauty has degrees, and lower forms remain within the category of beauty.
rows.anchor: لا سماجة ثمة لكن الحسن كغيره من المعاني على طبقات ومراتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implication of moving toward God is only an appearance relative to us and our time; ultimate reality excludes movement between sides because God is beyond direction and side.
rows.anchor: فإن نفس الأمر بمعزل عن حقيقة الانتقال من جانب إلى جانب إذا كان المنتقل إليه منزها عن الجانب وعن الجهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to Meccan disbelievers; the news points to worldly calamity they tasted and punishment prepared for the afterlife, and “taste” means the severity of their affair.
rows.anchor: خطاب لكفار مكة وذلك إشارة إلى الويل الذي ذاقوه في الدنيا وإلى ما أعد لهم من العذاب في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That is because” means the matter was that they objected to a human messenger guiding them; they did not object to worshipping stone idols, so they disbelieved and turned away.
rows.anchor: أنكروا أن يكون الرسول بشرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God had been independent of their obedience and worship from pre-eternity.
rows.anchor: واستغنى الله عن طاعتهم وعبادتهم من الأزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥamīd means either the one inherently deserving praise or the one who praises.
rows.anchor: والحميد بمعنى المحمود أي المستحق للحمد بذاته ويكون بمعنى الحامد

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī’s Kashshāf explains zaʿama as claiming to know something.
rows.anchor: في ( الكشاف ) : الزعيم ادعاء العلم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying calls “they claim” a mount for falsehood.
rows.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( زعموا مطية الكذب )

rows.speaker: شريح
rows.claim: Shurayḥ says everything has a nickname, and the nickname of lying is “they claim.”
rows.anchor: وعن شريح لكل شيء كنية وكنية الكذب زعموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zaʿama takes two objects like the verb “to know”; the cited poet’s line exemplifies its construction.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : ولم أزعمك عن ذلك معزولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers meant here are the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: والذين كفروا هم أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Balā affirms the proposition following the negative particle an, namely resurrection.
rows.anchor: { بلى } إثبات لما بعد أن وهو البعث

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes the command to swear as instruction to the Messenger, teaching him to use an oath to reinforce what he reports about resurrection, as with Quranic oaths generally.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون تعليما للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means nothing can impede resurrection; one explanation is that restoring people after they became dust is, to reason, easier than creating them initially.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن أمر البعث على الله يسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They turned away” is not redundant with “they disbelieved”: their rejection of human messengers expressed complete refusal and turning away, hence both verbs.
rows.anchor: وهذا في معنى الإنكار والإعراض بالكلية

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshāf explains the sequence as God’s independence becoming manifest when He did not compel them to faith, despite having power to do so.
rows.anchor: حيث لم يلجئهم إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although they deny his prophethood, they believe he holds his Lord in the highest regard and know he would swear only when the truth is as clear to him as daylight; the lām and nūn then intensify the assertion like an oath after an oath.
rows.anchor: أكد الخبر باللام والنون فكأنه قسم بعد قسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After strongly asserting resurrection, the discourse calls for belief in God and His Messenger because acknowledging resurrection is a requirement of faith.
rows.anchor: ولما بالغ في الإخبار عن البعث والاعتراف بالبعث من لوازم الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage notes readings تظاهرا, تتظاهرا, and سحران تظاهرا in the preceding discussion of the angels’ support.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { تظاهرا } و { * تتظاهرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other women could be better replacements if the Prophet divorced wives who disobeyed and harmed him, since they would no longer possess that quality while obedient replacements would.
rows.anchor: إذا طلقهن الرسول لعصيانهن له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam here is affirmation by the tongue and faith affirmation by the heart; they may diverge, so the paired descriptions confirm both.
rows.anchor: الإسلام هو التصديق باللسان والإيمان هو التصديق بالقلب

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshāf explains the conjunction before “previously married and virgins” because these mutually exclusive qualities cannot coexist as the other qualities can.
rows.anchor: لا يجتمعن فيهما اجتماعهن في سائر الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning previously married women as praise is no flaw: a widow may surpass some virgins for the Prophet by wealth, beauty, lineage, or a combination.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يكون البعض من الثيب خيرا بالنسبة إلى البعض من الأبكار عند الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Protect yourselves by refraining from what God has forbidden.
rows.anchor: بالانتهاء عما نهاكم الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says this means disciplining oneself and one’s family, enjoining good and forbidding evil.
rows.anchor: مقاتل : أن يؤدب المسلم نفسه وأهله

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshāf says to protect oneself by leaving sins and performing duties, and to protect one’s family by holding them accountable as oneself is held accountable.
rows.anchor: في ( الكشاف ) : { قوا أنفسكم } بترك المعاصي وفعل الطاعات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says to guard oneself against the soul’s promptings, since the soul commands evil.
rows.anchor: وقيل : { قوا أنفسكم } مما تدعو إليه أنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has nominative أهلوكم, coordinated with the wāw in ءامنوا قوا; the intervening words make the coordination acceptable.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : { * وأهلوكم } عطفا على واو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire is a kind whose fuel consists only of people and stones.
rows.anchor: نوعا من النار لا يتقد إلا بالناس والحجارة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the stones as sulfur, because it is among the hottest things when kindled.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس هي حجارة الكبريت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading has َوَقُودُهَا with ḍamma on the wāw.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : { وقودها } بالضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels over the Fire are the nineteen keepers and their assistants.
rows.anchor: يعني الزبانية التسعة عشر وأعوانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harshness and severity may describe their bodies, meaning coarseness and strength, or their actions, meaning roughness and force; either could characterize their nature or conduct.
rows.anchor: في أجرامهم غلظة وشدة أي جفاء وقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may be severe toward God’s enemies and merciful toward His allies, as another verse says.
rows.anchor: أشداء على أعداء الله ، رحماء على أولياء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their execution of commands explains their severity: pity does not stop them carrying out God’s orders or punishing His enemies.
rows.anchor: لا تأخذهم رأفة في تنفيذ أوامر الله تعالى والانتقام من أعدائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that angels are morally tasked in the afterlife with what God commands and forbids, and that disobedience means violating command or prohibition.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن الملائكة مكلفون في الآخرة بما أمرهم الله تعالى به وبما ينهاهم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are told to avoid sinful conduct that would place them alongside the disbelievers for whom the Fire was prepared; the command may also warn them against apostasy.
rows.anchor: باجتناب الفسق مجاورة الذين أعدت لهم هذه النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if sinful believers occupy a higher level than disbelievers, they share the same abode, which grounds the warning to protect oneself; avoiding apostasy may also be intended.
rows.anchor: فإنهم مع الكفار في دار واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since angels are spirits, Rāzī finds it more plausible that harshness and severity describe their qualities rather than their substance.
rows.anchor: وهذا أقرب بالنسبة إلى الغير من الأقوال

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshāf distinguishes the clauses: angels accept and adhere to God’s commands without denying them, then carry out what they are commanded.
rows.anchor: معنى الأول أنهم يتقبلون أوامره ويلتزمونها ولا ينكرونها ، ومعنى الثاني أنهم ( يؤدون ) ما يؤمرون به كذا ذكره في ( الكشاف )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned are told not to make excuses because here اعتذار means repentance, which is no longer accepted after entering the Fire.
rows.anchor: لا تعتذروا اليوم إذ الاعتذار هو التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their evil deeds entail punishment as required by divine wisdom.
rows.anchor: إنما أعمالكم السيئة ألزمتكم العذاب في الحكمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، مقاتل، السدي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Muqātil, and al-Suddī report that Nūn means a fish, invoking Dhū al-Nūn as a Quranic parallel.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول مروي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد ومقاتل والسدي

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some proponents take the fish to be the whale on whose back the earth rests in a sea beneath the lowest earth.
rows.anchor: منهم من قال : إنه قسم بالحوت الذي على ظهره الأرض

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others take it to be the whale that held Jonah in its belly.
rows.anchor: منهم من قال : إنه قسم بالحوت الذي احتبس يونس عليه السلام في بطنه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view identifies it as the whale that stained Nimrod’s arrow with its blood.
rows.anchor: منهم من قال : إنه قسم بالحوت الذي لطخ سهم نمروذ بدمه

rows.speaker: الضحاك، الحسن، قتادة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also transmitted, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda preferred, that Nūn means an inkwell; the poem uses nūn in that sense.
rows.anchor: واختيار الضحاك والحسن وقتادة أن النون هو الدواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Nūn means an inkwell, the oath pairs inkwell and pen because writing is greatly useful: communication comes through speech or writing.
rows.anchor: فإن التفاهم تارة يحصل بالنطق

rows.speaker: معاوية بن قرة
rows.claim: A report raised to the Prophet identifies Nūn as a tablet on which angels write what God commands them.
rows.anchor: أن النون لوح تكتب الملائكة ما يأمرهم الله به فيه رواه معاوية بن قرة مرفوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view takes Nūn as the ink with which the angels write.
rows.anchor: أن النون هو المداد الذي تكتب به الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed oath interpretations are weak on case grounds: a generic fish or inkwell should be indefinite and genitive, while a proper name should be declinable and genitive or indeclinable with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: هذه الوجوه ضعيفة لأنا إذا جعلناه مقسما به وجب إن كان جنسا أن نجره وننونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth view says Nūn is the final letter of al-Raḥmān and intends an oath by the whole name; Rāzī rejects it as opening the door to esoteric absurdities.
rows.anchor: وهذا أيضا ضعيف لأن تجويزه يفتح باب ترهات الباطنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī holds that Nūn is either the sūra’s name, a challenge, or one of the other explanations discussed at the opening of al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: بل الحق أنه إما أن يكون اسما للسورة أو يكون الغرض منه التحدي أو سائر الوجوه المذكورة في أول سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ over pronouncing the nūn distinctly or concealing it: pausing at the spelled letter requires clarity, while treating it as connected to the next word permits concealment.
rows.anchor: القراء مختلفون في إظهار النون وإخفائه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ prefers distinct pronunciation because the letter is spelled out and spelled letters are treated like paused forms even when connected.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : وإظهارها أعجب إلي لأنها هجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the oath’s pen generically to mean every pen used in heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: القسم به هو الجنس وهو واقع على كل قلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic pen recalls God’s gift of writing as well as speech: writing lets a person communicate with someone distant as speech does with someone present.
rows.anchor: ووجه الانتفاع به أن ينزل الغائب منزلة المخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view identifies the oath’s pen as the particular pen mentioned in the report that it was the first thing God created.
rows.anchor: أن المقسم به هو القلم المعهود الذي جاء في الخبر أن أول ما خلق الله القلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that God first created the pen, ordered it to record all events until the Hour, and it wrote lifespans and deeds; it is a pen of light spanning heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : أول ما خلق الله القلم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that the first-created pen wrote destiny through the Day of Resurrection, so people proceed according to a decree already completed.
rows.anchor: وروى مجاهد عنه قال : أول ما خلق الله القلم

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qāḍī reads the pen report metaphorically: a writing tool cannot be a living, responsible being; rather, God’s power brings all events to pass without resistance, like “Be, and it is.”
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : هذا الخبر يجب حمله على المجاز

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: Some identify the pen with the intellect, the source of created things, and infer that it is one with the primordial jewel described in another report.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من زعم أن القلم المذكور ههنا هو العقل

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: Their second report says the first creation was a jewel; God regarded it with awe, it melted and heated, and smoke and foam arose, from which heaven and earth were made respectively.
rows.anchor: وفي خبر آخر : أول ما خلق الله تعالى جوهرة

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: They combine the reports by identifying the pen, intellect, and primordial jewel as one thing, arguing that otherwise the reports would contradict each other.
rows.anchor: فهذه الأخبار بمجموعها تدل على أن القلم والعقل وتلك الجوهرة التي هي أصل المخلوقات شيء واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase with mā can function as a verbal noun meaning their writing, or refer to what is written; either reading makes the writing or written material the object of the oath.
rows.anchor: ما مع ما بعدها في تقدير المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pen means all pens in creation, God swears by every pen and everything written by every pen.
rows.anchor: وكأنه تعالى أقسم بكل قلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes what is written to be what the guardian angels and noble scribes record.
rows.anchor: وقيل : بل المراد ما يسطره الحفظة والكرام الكاتبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word “pen” may stand for its writers, making the pronoun in “they write” refer to pen-owners and their written records.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالقلم أصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pen is the particular primordial pen, “what they write” may mean the Preserved Tablet on which it writes; the plural is honorific, not literal.
rows.anchor: أي وما يسطرون فيه وهو اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means everything recorded on the Preserved Tablet: deeds, lifespans, and all events through the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: الأشياء التي سطرت فيه من الأعمال والأعمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning the objects of the oath, God states what is sworn: the Prophet is not mad, will have an undiminished reward, and has exalted character.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر المقسم به أتبعه بذكر المقسم عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās relates that the Prophet went to Ḥirāʾ and Khadīja searched for him; he told her Gabriel brought the first revelation, taught him ablution and prayer, and she consulted her Christian cousin Waraqa, who promised support but died before the call; Quraysh then called the Prophet mad.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه عليه السلام غاب عن خديجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says God swore the Prophet was not mad in response to the Quraysh accusation, and identifies this as the first five verses of the sūra.
rows.anchor: فأقسم الله تعالى على أنه ليس بمجنون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also says the first revelation was “Glorify the name of your Lord Most High,” making this verse the second revelation.
rows.anchor: وأول ما نزل قوله : { سبح اسم ربك }

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses anta as the subject noun of mā and bimajnūn as its predicate; biniʿmati rabbik is parenthetical.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : { أنت } هو اسم { ما }

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the phrase as saying that madness is absent through God’s grace, as in expressions that attribute intelligence or freedom from poverty to God’s blessing.
rows.anchor: انتفى عنك الجنون بنعمة ربك

rows.speaker: عطاء وابن عباس
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and Ibn ʿAbbās say the blessing means the faith and prophethood bestowed on the Messenger, answering those who called him mad.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء وابن عباس : يريد بنعمة ربك عليك بالإيمان والنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s visible gifts to the Prophet—eloquence, complete intellect, commendable conduct, freedom from defects, and possession of virtues—are incompatible with madness and expose the accusers as liars.
rows.anchor: نعم الله تعالى كانت ظاهرة في حقه من الفصاحة التامة والعقل الكامل والسيرة المرضية

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most interpreters take ghayr mamnūn to mean an unshortened, undiminished reward; the root can mean weakening or cutting off, as in Labīd’s verse about prey dogs whose food is not withheld.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الأكثرين ، أن المعنى غير منقوص ولا مقطوع

rows.speaker: مجاهد، مقاتل، الكلبي
rows.claim: Mujāhid, Muqātil, and al-Kalbī explain the reward as not conditioned by a favor or obligation; the Muʿtazilites say it is deserved recompense for the Prophet’s work, not an initial gift.
rows.anchor: قول مجاهد ومقاتل والكلبي ، إنه غير مقدر عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers the meaning “uninterrupted and undiminished,” since calling it a reward already implies that it carries no favor; the alternative would repeat itself.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أشبه لأن وصفه بأنه أجر يفيد أنه لا منة فيه فالحمل على هذا الوجه يكون كالتكرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the reward is for enduring the slander and offensive accusations, and is great and lasting.
rows.anchor: قال قوم معناه : إن لك على احتمال هذا الطعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others say the lasting, pure reward is for proclaiming prophethood and miracles, calling people to God, and explaining the law; it should encourage the Prophet to continue this vital work despite accusations.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : المراد إن لك في إظهار النبوة والمعجزات
